expectations.text: Output identifies 5 or more distinct domains affected
expectations.evidence: 4 loosely-defined areas identified: Performance, Code Quality, Learning Curve/Hiring, Ecosystem/Migration. These are not structured as distinct stakeholder domains. Missing: Customers, Regulators, Internal Knowledge, Product Velocity, Competitive Position

expectations.text: Output traces at least 2 orders of effects beyond first-order for the majority of domains
expectations.evidence: All effects are first-order only. No explicit second or third-order effects traced. Bullet points list direct consequences without exploring causal chains (e.g., 'hiring challenges' is stated but not traced to what happens BECAUSE of hiring challenges)

expectations.text: Output identifies at least 2 feedback loops with mechanism explanations
expectations.evidence: Zero feedback loops identified. No circular causal dynamics described. All effects are presented as linear, independent consequences

expectations.text: Output labels feedback loops as amplifying or dampening
expectations.evidence: No feedback loops present, so no labeling possible

expectations.text: Output is structured with clear domain-by-domain organization
expectations.evidence: Organized by positive/negative effects and cost considerations, not by stakeholder domain. This groups effects by valence (good/bad) rather than by who is affected

expectations.text: Output includes at least 1 counter-intuitive or non-obvious effect
expectations.evidence: All effects listed are conventional/obvious (learning curve, hiring difficulty, ecosystem maturity, migration risk). No surprising or non-obvious dynamics identified

expectations.text: Output provides mechanisms (why/because) for causal chains, not just listing effects
expectations.evidence: Effects are stated without mechanisms. E.g., 'Rust developers are much harder to find than Java developers' — no explanation of what happens because of this or why the market is structured this way
